content.comment_body: I have a site with 9 programmable controllers. 3 use an older [version_no], and 6 use a newer [version_no]. Periodically, the 6 controllers with the newer [version_no] freeze—remaining stuck in their last operating state, such as heating being stuck on. This happened once after about a month of programming, and then again after around 3 months. None of the 3 older controllers have this issue, even though one runs the same program as one of the newer ones.

I am only aware of errors involving the [version_no] hardware variation, where the display freezes and responds only after a restart. In your situation, I would suggest returning the affected controllers. There is a newer hardware revision ([version_no]), where this issue should not occur.

Yes, it’s the [version_no] hardware and yes, they only respond to power cycling. I haven’t seen this issue with any previous version. How can I confirm if they are standard [version_no], or a newer revision? All I know is that the earlier hardware label showed [version_no], and the ones that freeze show [version_no] on the label.

Apologies, English is not my first language so I may miss some details or make spelling errors. Due to various issues with the [version_no] hardware, a new revision has been released. Additionally, there is a service pack for the related configuration software ([product_name] [version_no]), since there were also errors with the software. Installing the service pack will update to [version_no].
Do you think reprogramming the [version_no] controllers with the new configuration software will resolve the freezing problem?
I don’t think it will help. Consider returning your controller or submitting a support request.
Thank you for the recommendation. I will open a support request. Thanks again.
Hello [user_name], please check out this topic: Product information on [product_name] hardware revisions and errors.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering intermittent freezing issues with newer revisions of [product_name] controllers, specifically those with [version_no] hardware, causing the devices to stop responding and maintaining the last active state until restarted. This problem does not affect older hardware versions, even when running identical programs. The freezing disrupts operations—for example, heating remains on until reset. A possible solution involves updating to a newer hardware revision and applying a service pack for the related configuration software, as instability affects both hardware and software versions mentioned.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent and reliable performance from newer [product_name] controller revisions, matching the reliability of earlier versions without unexpected freezing or the need for manual intervention.
